tasks.short: Lead systems projects, coordinate technical work, and supervise programmers or analysts.

steps.what: Review milestones, assignments, dependencies, and overdue work.
Collect missing updates and consolidate reported blockers.

loop.input: Updates submitted for the current project reporting period.
loop.output: Blockers, dependencies, reported owners, and missing information with source references.
loop.check: Validate project identifiers and dates; the project lead checks ambiguous ownership and unsupported interpretations.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per update; unresolved items return to the project lead.
loop.why_not_simpler: Current updates contain free text whose wording varies. Structured forms can replace extraction where adopted.

steps.what: Assess technical dependencies, delivery risks, and sequencing options.
Agree priorities and approve changes beyond delegated scope or capacity.
Coach team members, resolve disagreements, and agree practical next actions.
Update assignments, dates, dependencies, and decisions in project records.
Prepare and circulate the project progress report.

tasks.design: Configure a delivery dashboard and structured decision and action records in the {PROJECT}, with approved changes updating assignments automatically. A bounded loop extracts blockers from submitted updates in the {EMAIL} and {CHAT}; a deterministic template produces a progress report in the {DOCS} for review. Technical tradeoffs, sponsor decisions, and coaching remain human.
tasks.previous_blocker: Updates arrive in different formats, and decisions made in meetings require repeated entry. Existing reporting also depends on consistent project records.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured views and workflows handle much of the work. Coding assistance can reduce the effort of connecting records and generating reports; bounded extraction handles free-text updates.
tasks.still_hard: Incomplete updates, hidden dependencies, and conflicting commitments remain difficult. Employee information needs restricted access under GDPR; monitoring changes may require consultation under national rules and assessment under the EU AI Act.
tasks.human_edge: Notice when apparent delivery problems reflect uncertainty, overloaded colleagues, or unresolved disagreement, and secure credible commitments.
tasks.altitude: Less time goes into chasing updates and assembling reports; more goes into coaching and resolving dependencies. With explicit sponsor delegation, the project lead can resequence work within agreed capacity between formal steering meetings.

reach.task: Forecast delivery risk across several systems projects.
reach.learn: Dependency modelling, capacity planning, and forecast calibration.

reach.task: Investigate recurring handoff delays between operational teams.
reach.learn: Process observation, root-cause analysis, and outcome measurement.

evidence.claim: Configured project records, dashboards, and structured approvals can remove repeated status assembly and record entry.
Free-text summarisation and reviewed drafting are available in service-management software; this supports the bounded-loop pattern, not autonomous supervision.
Coding assistance supports implementation and review, with human oversight expected.
A randomised developer study found slower completion with AI assistance, so faster construction cannot be assumed.

assumptions: Steps and time shares describe an illustrative mid-size European company, not measured customer activity.
Build ranges cover one project team and one reporting process; they are working-effort estimates, not consultation calendar durations.
Structured decisions and agreed actions are the source for automatic record updates.
The design excludes employee scoring and broad collection of private messages.
unknowns: Which reporting and approval features the current {PROJECT} supports.
Whether project records contain reliable owners, dates, and dependencies.
Who can approve scope changes and delegate sequencing decisions.
Which employee consultation requirements apply under national rules.
Whether access to submitted updates and project interfaces is available.
research_questions: Which missing updates can be replaced by existing work-record events?
Can structured blocker forms remove the need for text extraction?
Does a pilot reduce preparation time without hiding emerging delivery risks?
new_work: Review extracted blockers and resolve ambiguous ownership.
Handle failed updates and conflicting edits.
Maintain report templates, workflow rules, and access permissions.
Check that reporting supports coordination without becoming employee scoring.

tasks.short: Prepare cost-benefit and return-on-investment analyses for proposed systems investments.

steps.what: Confirm the problem, alternatives, analysis horizon, and intended business outcomes.
Export current operating costs, transaction volumes, and project effort.
Collect proposals and identify implementation, subscription, migration, and support costs.

loop.input: Supplier proposals and internal estimates for the agreed alternatives.
loop.output: Source-linked cost items with currency, charging period, exclusions, and uncertain terms.
loop.check: Validate numeric fields and units; the analyst checks material costs and all ambiguous terms against sources.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per document; missing or conflicting terms remain flagged for clarification.
loop.why_not_simpler: Proposals describe charging terms and exclusions in varying prose and layouts. Standard cost forms should bypass the loop.

steps.what: Set benefit assumptions, adoption scenarios, risks, and treatment of released staff time.
Calculate cash flows, return, payback, and sensitivity across alternatives.
Write the business case, recommendation, uncertainties, and comparison of alternatives.

loop.input: Validated scenario tables, source references, assumptions, and the analyst's chosen recommendation.
loop.output: Business-case narrative linked to calculated results and stated uncertainties.
loop.check: Insert financial tables deterministically; verify narrative numbers against results and require analyst review of causal claims.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; unsupported claims are removed and unresolved sections return to the analyst.
loop.why_not_simpler: Project-specific explanations connect qualitative risks and benefits. Fixed templates can handle routine cases without a loop.

steps.what: Challenge assumptions with finance and approve, defer, or reject the investment.

tasks.design: A versioned calculator on the {DATA_PLATFORM} combines approved exports from the {ERP}, {OPS_SYSTEM}, and {PROJECT} with an assumption register, then generates a financial model and scenario tables. Bounded loops extract source-linked proposal terms and draft the business case in the {DOCS}; the analyst reviews both. Finance challenges the assumptions, and the investment sponsor approves the investment.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each analysis combines different proposals, cost definitions, and benefit assumptions. Reusable calculations were possible, but source mapping and document preparation remained bespoke.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable calculation code, validation rules, and document templates can be built with coding assistance. Small extraction and drafting loops handle variable prose without controlling the financial calculations.
tasks.still_hard: Attributing benefits, estimating adoption, and distinguishing released capacity from cash savings remain judgement calls. Missing baseline data can dominate uncertainty even when arithmetic is correct.
tasks.human_edge: Challenge optimistic benefits, expose who must change behaviour, and explain when a strategically useful investment has weak measurable returns.

ambition.what: Quarterly benefits-realisation review for completed systems investments

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends less time rebuilding models and more time testing assumptions with operational owners. They can propose corrective scenarios during benefits reviews; investment approval remains with the sponsor.

reach.task: Measure whether a new system changed process costs and outcomes.
reach.learn: Baseline design, benefit attribution, and measurement of adoption.

reach.task: Update investment forecasts when delivery scope or timing changes.
reach.learn: Forecast maintenance, contingency treatment, and benefits dependencies.

evidence.claim: Cash-flow calculations, scenario comparisons, and document tables can be generated deterministically from explicit assumptions.
Prompted document metadata extraction exists, with explicit warnings that extracted values may be wrong.
Coding assistance can support construction of calculation and reporting tools, with oversight.
Developer field trials found higher task completion with assistance, but do not establish a comparable speedup for a complete financial-analysis workflow.

assumptions: Steps and time shares describe a typical investment analysis, not measured customer activity.
Build ranges cover one reusable model, a limited set of data interfaces, and one business-case template.
Financial formulas execute as deterministic code; models do not invent costs, discount rates, or benefits.
Aggregate operational data is preferred. Personal-data use needs GDPR assessment, and employee monitoring or evaluation requires assessment under the EU AI Act and national rules.
Consent and access estimates include initial consultation work where applicable; statutory or negotiated waiting periods can extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Which financial metrics, discount rates, and approval thresholds finance requires.
Whether baseline cost, volume, and effort data can be reconciled.
Whether supplier proposals are available in readable formats.
Which benefits have accountable operational owners and measurable baselines.
Whether personal data is necessary and national consultation rules apply.
Which source interfaces and document-generation permissions are available.
research_questions: Which existing calculation template can be configured before building a new calculator?
Which claimed time savings produce cash savings, usable capacity, or service improvements?
Can reviewers trace every material figure from the business case to its source and assumption?
How closely do completed investments match their original benefit scenarios?
new_work: Review extracted costs, exclusions, charging periods, and ambiguous terms.
Maintain calculation rules, model versions, and source mappings.
Check narrative claims against calculated results.
Refresh assumptions when scope, adoption, or delivery timing changes.
Compare realised outcomes with the approved business case.

role.altitude: The systems analyst shifts from assembling updates and financial documents toward resolving delivery constraints and challenging investment assumptions. Broader sequencing rights require sponsor delegation; financial commitments remain subject to investment approval.
reach: Information technology project manager: forecast dependencies and delivery risk across projects.
Management analyst: measure operational benefits after implementation.
Project management specialist: maintain investment forecasts as delivery plans change.
skills_to_grow: Deterministic financial modelling and data validation
GDPR-aware access design and national consultation requirements
role.ambitious_version: Run a repeatable investment-to-outcome service that connects each systems proposal to delivery decisions, adoption evidence, and quarterly benefits reviews.
